Latitude

LAT-ih-tood — in this unit, forget the lines on a map; latitude here means room to roam freely in your choices. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Latitude is scope for freedom of action or thought.

The director gave the actors considerable latitude to improvise their own lines during the scene.

Worked Example

A new employee expects to be told exactly how to format every single report. Instead, her boss simply says, 'Use whatever approach makes sense to you, as long as the numbers are accurate' — and never questions her methods again.

Being trusted with real freedom to choose your own approach, without being micromanaged, is exactly what latitude means. Unlike 'permission,' which is a one-time yes, latitude is an ongoing, broad freedom to act as you see fit.

How Latitude Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

freedom

freedom: the power to act as one wishes

leeway

leeway: room to move or act within a situation

flexibility

flexibility: the ability to adapt or choose different approaches

Antonyms

restriction

restriction: a limitation on what is allowed

constraint

constraint: something that limits freedom of action

How Strong Is It? — leeway → latitude → autonomy

leeway vs. latitude

leeway vs. latitude: Leeway is a slightly smaller, more casual version of latitude — leeway often covers small, everyday flexibility, while latitude implies a broader, more significant scope of freedom.

autonomy vs. latitude

autonomy vs. latitude: Autonomy can go even further than latitude: latitude means being given room to make choices within a system, but autonomy means having full independent control over the whole decision.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — -lat-

root — -lat-: wide, broad (Latin (latus))

suffix — -itude

suffix — -itude: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin latus meant 'wide, broad.' Latitude, at its root, is the state of having broad room to move — first used for the wide east-west bands on a map, and later for the broad, figurative room a person has to act as they choose.

Use the root in a new word: dilate

Use the root in a new word: dilate: In the dark theater, her pupils began to dilate to let in more light.
